title: Premise checks must survive serialization; unverifiable premises fail-safe
context: v1.10.7 shipped a silent fail-open: hunch_record_decision advertised nested premises shape but PremiseSchema is flat. Zod silently stripped the check during storage. Any premise recorded through the documented API could never fire, violating the core invariant that unverifiable premises are never held.
decision: Enforce that premise checks are serialized durably and always evaluated. Unverifiable data (missing checks, unparseable clocks) cannot satisfy a premise—fail-safe, not fail-open. Add mandatory regression test that fails if checks are ever stripped again.
consequences: All v1.10.7 premises must be re-recorded; stored records have no check attached
Premise evaluation now guaranteed to fail-safe on unparseable input
Release process must pin version in all three locations (package.json, plugin/.mcp.json, server.json) or pipeline fails
Fail-safe semantics now consistent across the feature
alternatives_rejected: Keep schema mismatch; treat checked premises as plain notes without checks
Continue fail-open pattern where unparseable clocks default to holds=true
Manual documentation of version sites instead of enforcing comprehensive updates
